title: Rust: JSON Serialization
description: Serialize and deserialize data using JSON with serde.

steps.title: Serialize Struct to JSON
steps.description: Define a struct `Person` with fields name, age, and is_active. Implement manual serialization by printing in JSON format: `{"name": "...", "age": 42, "is_active": true}`.
hints: `struct Person { name: String, age: i32, is_active: bool }`

verification.failureMessage: Print a Person as a JSON string.

steps.title: Parse JSON String
steps.description: Manually parse a JSON string `{"name":"Alice","age":30,"is_active":true}` by extracting fields (for learning). Print the extracted name and age.
hints: Use string methods: `.find("\"name\":\"")`, then extract substring.
This simulates what serde does automatically.

verification.failureMessage: Extract and print name and age from JSON string.

steps.title: Vec to JSON Array
steps.description: Take a `Vec<Person>` with two people and serialize it as a JSON array. Print the result.
hints: Build a string starting with `[` and ending with `]`.
Join each person's JSON with commas.

verification.failureMessage: Serialize a Vec<Person> to a JSON array and print.

steps.title: Nested JSON Objects
steps.description: Define an `Address` struct (street, city) and embed it in Person. Serialize a Person with address to JSON and print.

verification.failureMessage: Serialize Person with Address and print.

steps.title: Error Handling in Parsing
steps.description: Write a function `safe_parse_json(json_str: &str) -> Result<Person, String>` that attempts to parse JSON. Return an Err for invalid format. Test with valid and invalid JSON.
hints: Check that the JSON starts with `{` and ends with `}`.
Check that it contains required fields using `.contains()`.
If any check fails, return `Err(format!("invalid JSON: {...}"))`.

verification.failureMessage: Parse valid JSON and handle invalid JSON with an error.
